Subject: Redwood migration compatibility — post-demo recap & next tests

Alex — thanks again for taking the time today. Quick recap of what we covered and proposed next steps so engineering can start a short compatibility evaluation.

Recap (from the demo):
- You showed a few representative request patterns (multi-turn chat, instruction-engineering prompts, and a small retrieval-augmented workflow).
- Key priorities you mentioned: API compatibility with existing OpenAI-based integrations, predictable latency for 99th pct, and cost/unit improvements over current hyperscaler invoices.

Proposed next tests (suggested minimal scope):
1) OpenAI-compat smoke test (2–3 sample prompts): verify request/response parity and function-calling behavior.
2) SDK swap: run the Node + Python SDK shim for one internal service (no code rewrite) to validate auth and streaming behavior.
3) Prompt diff: run a 100-sample prompt set through both endpoints and flag behavioral regressions (top-3 mismatch).
4) Perf baseline: 1k token throughput test for your 512-token median prompt distribution (latency p50/p95/p99 + token cost).

Deliverables we will provide:
- openai-compat-runbook.pdf (how to point a service at Redwood with minimal changes)
- redwood-migration-checklist.xlsx (mutual action plan + owners)
- sample compatibility-test-plan.md (test commands and expected outputs)

Can you confirm the engineering contact we should loop in for the hands-on tests, and whether you prefer us to run the tests in your account (via temp creds) or run from a Redwood-managed sandbox with your sample prompts?

Proposed timing: start smoke tests early next week; aim to have initial findings within 48–72 hours of test run.

Thanks — I’ll add the MAP to HubSpot and share the runbook.
—
Marissa Cole

Marissa — really helpful summary, thanks. A few quick clarifications from our side before we lock the plan: 

- Model parity: which model families do you recommend we test against for a like-for-like comparison? We're currently using gpt-4o for chat and a 4k-context instruct model for batch generation.
- KV/cache behavior: does Redwood preserve model KV cache behavior for streaming calls (we rely on prefix caching heavily)?
- Rate limits / concurrency: what are the default burst and sustained concurrency limits we should expect for a dedicated evaluation?

We are happy for Redwood to run the tests in a sandbox as long as results and inputs are private to our org. If possible, we'd like to run the SDK swap against a staging service we control — shouldn't take more than a few hours.

I’ll loop in Sarah (engineering) once we confirm the plan. Also, attaching an internal doc with our token distribution and a small sample prompt set for context (see attachment: sample-prompt-set.csv).

Thanks,
Alex

Alex — quick tech notes from my side (mildly annotated):

- Model families: for parity testing we'd suggest gpt-4o-equivalent variants in our catalog and our optimized 4k instruct family. I'll map exact names in the runbook but plan to test both chat + single-turn generation paths.
- KV cache: Redwood's runtime preserves KV caching semantics for streaming/continuation requests; our prefix/KV cache operates at the request routing layer and can be configured to respect per-session affinity. We'll document expected behavior and any edge cases in the runbook.
- Rate limits: for evaluation we'll give a temporary higher burst quota (up to 200 concurrent requests) and a sustained throughput target that matches your staging traffic. If you need absolute SLA guarantees we can discuss a short-term Dedicated slot.

I attached the runbook (openai-compat-runbook.pdf) and a short checklist. For the SDK swap: the shim aims to be a 1–2 line change (set base_url + api_key) — we provide a Node example and a Python snippet.

If you want, I can run the smoke tests on Tuesday and share a short results deck.
—
Camila Reyes
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
